home.latest.title: What’s new, and what we’re writing.
home.release.text: Each app release comes with the runtime it was tested with. The app tells you when a new one is ready, and updates your comma’s runtime from Device settings.
home.faq.title: Good to know.
home.faq.text: The short answers. Every guide has its own questions at the end.
home.faq.needA: An Android phone or tablet (Android 8 or later) and a comma 3X or comma four running openpilot or a supported fork, both on the same local network: your Wi-Fi, a hotspot from your phone, head unit or AI box, or the comma’s own. For setup you also need a GitHub account: the comma takes SSH keys from it, and CommaView makes the key.
home.faq.devicesQ: Which comma devices does CommaView work with?
home.faq.devicesA: The comma 3X and the comma four. Both run the same openpilot releases and forks, so CommaView works the same on either. The app runs on an Android phone, tablet or head unit.
home.faq.forksQ: Which openpilot forks does CommaView work with?
home.faq.forksA: openpilot, sunnypilot, StarPilot, xnor-tech’s openpilot (its xnor and rx builds), AdventurePilot, SunnyPilot-TeslaHW1, carrotpilot, BluePilot, dragonpilot and OPGM. Live View draws each fork’s own screen, with what that fork adds to it. Other openpilot forks work best effort: setup checks the fork and asks you before it installs.
home.faq.comma3A: comma moved the comma 3 to its own long-term release, openpilot 0.10, which has been frozen since September 2025, and sunnypilot has deprecated it. On that release the comma 3 draws its screen with openpilot’s older UI, which CommaView’s runtime can’t hook into to show the driving overlay. comma’s own tools still work on a comma 3; if that changes upstream, we’ll take another look.
home.faq.connectQ: How is it different from comma connect?
home.faq.connectA: They do different jobs, and you can use both. comma connect is comma’s web app: it keeps your uploaded drives and, since openpilot 0.11.2, can stream the cameras while the car is parked, over the internet. CommaView works on your own network: Live View shows the road camera with your fork’s driving overlay while you drive, and recordings go from the comma to your phone, with no upload and no subscription.
home.faq.connectLink: comma connect and CommaView, side by side
home.faq.screensQ: Does it work on a tablet or my car’s screen?
home.faq.screensA: Yes, on any Android tablet or Android head unit with Android 8 or later, and on an Android AI box on a car’s CarPlay or Android Auto screen. A car with a web browser, a Tesla’s too, can show Live View with Browser View.
home.faq.internetA: Live View and recordings don’t: they go straight from the comma to your phone. Signing in, app and runtime updates, your car’s picture, the map, routes, Go live and anything you send or contribute to CommaView do.
home.faq.commaA: No. CommaView is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by comma.ai.
home.faq.inviteA: Join the list. We’re letting people in in small groups and email each invite. Already invited? Sign in at my.commaview.com with the address your invite came to, and download the app there.
home.cta.title: Get your invite.
home.cta.lede: CommaView is invite-only while it’s in beta. Join the list and we’ll email you when it’s your turn.
home.cta.support: CommaView is independent and paid for out of pocket. {link} to help cover hosting, testing and the iOS app.

forks.title: Which openpilot forks work with CommaView
forks.description: CommaView works with openpilot, sunnypilot, StarPilot, xnor, AdventurePilot, SunnyPilot-TeslaHW1 and carrotpilot. What each fork shows in Live View.
forks.heading: openpilot, and the forks you drive with.
forks.lede: CommaView shows your comma’s road camera with the driving overlay of the software it runs. It works with openpilot and six of its forks, on the comma 3X and comma four, and, best effort, with [other openpilot forks](#unlisted).
forks.setupChecks: Guided setup checks which repository your comma’s software was installed from, and installs CommaView’s hook for that fork. On a fork it doesn’t list, setup checks whether CommaView can add its view and asks you first ([forks CommaView doesn’t list](#unlisted)); where it can’t, setup stops and leaves your comma as it was.
forks.unlisted1: From CommaView 0.0.165, with its runtime on your comma, setup can add CommaView’s view to an openpilot fork it doesn’t list, best effort. It checks the fork first, without changing anything. If CommaView can add its view, setup shows **CommaView hasn’t verified this fork**, names the fork by its repository and says what is drawn (the cameras, the path, lanes, the car ahead, alerts and speed) and what isn’t (the fork’s own buttons, colours and widgets). **Install anyway** installs on that fork, and only that one.
forks.unlisted2: Live View draws the fork in openpilot’s look, or sunnypilot’s when the fork builds on sunnypilot’s screen, and the app names it, such as “crwusiz/openpilot · best effort”. To undo it, Uninstall runtime in Device settings puts the fork’s files back as they were.
forks.unlistedBestEffort: **Best effort.** CommaView’s releases aren’t checked against your fork. If the fork updates itself into something CommaView can’t follow, CommaView’s view turns off and your fork drives and shows its own screen as usual, until a CommaView release handles the change.
forks.unlistedNotEvery: **Not every fork.** Forks built on openpilot’s older native screen aren’t supported ([which, and why](#not-supported)). When the check refuses a fork, setup says “CommaView can’t add its view to … safely” and “Nothing on your comma was changed.”
forks.unlistedYes: **Your yes is for that fork.** If your comma switches to another fork CommaView doesn’t list, CommaView asks again in setup before it adds its view there.
forks.checkTitle: Forks that pass the install check (best effort)
forks.check1: From CommaView 0.0.165, CommaView supports more openpilot forks, best effort: setup adds its view to a fork it doesn’t list once you agree.
forks.check2: Each of these **passes CommaView’s install check; best effort, not tested on a car.** Checked November 2026, for the branches named, against the runtime CommaView 0.0.165 installs: the installer offers the fork, adds CommaView’s view once you agree, and checks it, as it would on your comma. Nothing here was tried on a comma in a car, a fork may not support every car on both devices, and a fork’s next update can change the answer.
forks.checkLabel: Table of forks that pass the install check
forks.checkMissing: Your fork isn’t here? It may still work: setup checks it before it changes anything.
forks.notSupportedLede: These forks’ screens can’t take CommaView’s view, so setup says so and changes nothing on your comma:
forks.why.frogpilot: It runs openpilot’s older native (Qt) screen, which has no place for CommaView’s view.
forks.why.kisapilot: Its Python screen is switched off: it runs openpilot’s older native (Qt) screen.
forks.why.iqpilot: Since October 2026 it runs on its own IQ.OS; support waits until CommaView can support it as a fork of its own.
forks.why.hikee9123: It runs openpilot’s older native (Qt) screen.
forks.videoOnlyLink: Video only is in early access.
forks.videoOnlyWill: With the Video only flag, setup offers to play their cameras in Live View with CommaView’s own overlay in place of their own screens, changing nothing in the fork. It hasn’t been tried on a comma yet.
forks.videoOnlyWithout: Without the flag, setup still says they aren’t supported and changes nothing.
forks.devices: The comma 3X and the comma four. The comma 3 isn’t supported, including the forks’ comma 3 builds such as xnor-c3: [why the comma 3 isn’t supported]({comma3}). The app runs on an Android phone, tablet or head unit.
forks.branches: Before each release, CommaView’s runtime is built and checked against these forks’ release builds. openpilot’s nightly and sunnypilot’s dev branches are checked each day they change, as an early warning. A development branch can change faster than CommaView: if a change stops CommaView’s hook from loading, your fork’s screen and driving carry on as usual.
forks.request: Try it [best effort](#unlisted), and ask for it to be listed on the feature board at [my.commaview.com]({account}), or send an idea from the app (Settings › Support & diagnostics). A listed fork is checked before each release. Follow the [setup guide]({setup}), and see [what’s new]({whatsNew}) in each release.
forks.faq.sunnypilotA: Yes. CommaView draws sunnypilot’s screen with what sunnypilot adds, from MADS and speed-limit assist to the rainbow path and blind-spot indicators, on the comma 3X and comma four.
forks.faq.starpilotA: Yes, from CommaView 0.0.162. Live View shows StarPilot’s own colours, widgets and camera choice. Turn off StarPilot’s Disable Logging setting, which stops the video encoder CommaView streams from.
forks.faq.xnorQ: Does CommaView work with xnor-tech’s openpilot?
forks.faq.xnorA: Yes, from CommaView 0.0.163, both its xnor and rx builds. xnor runs openpilot’s screen and rx runs sunnypilot’s, and CommaView draws whichever your comma runs. On a Rivian, the wheel turns green while the car steers by angle and blue while it steers by torque.
forks.faq.adventurepilotA: Yes, from CommaView 0.0.163. It draws sunnypilot’s screen with AdventurePilot’s lane-centering indicator, its CURVE chip on the comma 3X screen and its steering mode’s wheel tint.
forks.faq.teslahw1A: Yes, from CommaView 0.0.164. It’s a sunnypilot fork for Tesla’s HW1 cars, and CommaView draws sunnypilot’s screen for it, with everything sunnypilot adds.
forks.faq.carrotpilotA: Yes, from CommaView 0.0.164. Live View draws openpilot’s screen for it; what carrotpilot adds to its own screen, such as its navigation and speed cameras, isn’t drawn yet. After carrotpilot updates itself, the app asks for a reboot that brings Live View back.
forks.faq.newestQ: Does CommaView work with BluePilot, dragonpilot or OPGM?
forks.faq.newestA: Yes, from CommaView 0.0.166 with its runtime. CommaView names each and draws it in its base’s look: BluePilot as sunnypilot, dragonpilot and OPGM as openpilot, with dragonpilot’s ALKA shown as steering. A comma that ran one best effort moves to it at the boot after the runtime update. None has been driven with CommaView yet. CommaView’s official overlay packs draw more of BluePilot’s and dragonpilot’s own screens.
forks.faq.otherQ: Does CommaView work with FrogPilot or another fork?
forks.faq.otherA: Not FrogPilot: it runs openpilot’s older native (Qt) screen, which has no place for CommaView’s view, so setup says it isn’t supported and changes nothing.{videoOnly} Other openpilot forks work best effort from CommaView 0.0.165: setup checks the fork without changing anything and, if CommaView can add its view, says what will and won’t be drawn and installs only when you agree. crwusiz, zoompilot, jixiexiaoge’s Carrot and more pass CommaView’s install check; best effort, not tested on a car. From CommaView 0.0.166, BluePilot, dragonpilot and OPGM are listed forks. Ask for your fork on the feature board at my.commaview.com to have it checked before each release.
forks.faq.videoOnlySoon: Video only is in early access for {forks}, for testers. {will}
forks.faq.drivingQ: Does CommaView change how my fork drives?
forks.faq.drivingA: No. It adds a small runtime beside your fork and a small hook in its on-screen UI, so CommaView can draw the same path, lanes and alerts. How your car drives doesn’t change.

team.title: Team | CommaView
team.heading: Who builds CommaView.
team.lede: CommaView is made by RhynoTech, a one-person company: its founder designs, builds and supports it, with AI coding tools as part of the engineering.
team.founder.bio: Ryan founded CommaView through RhynoTech and builds every part of it: the Android app, the runtime on the comma device, the overlay pack SDK, the account service and this site. Ryan works closely with the openpilot community, keeping CommaView working across many openpilot forks, and uses AI coding tools as part of the engineering.
